newsitem.title: USA: CINergy says wins rate increase from state.
newsitem.headline: CINergy says wins rate increase from state.

text.p: The Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission approved an overall average 7.4-percent rate increase for PSI Energy, said parent firm CINergy Corp.
The rate increase was originally requested to be 12.8 percent, the company said.
The average residential customer using 1,000 kilowatt hours of electricity monthly will see an increase of 8.7 percent or $5.56 per month in his power bill, it said.

The majority of the $73.9-million increase in annual revenue will go to pay for projects such as a coal gasification plant in Terre Haute, Ind.; energy efficiency programs to cut demand for electricity; a scrubber at PSI's Gibson Station near Princeton, Ind.; and basic equipment such as electrical transformers, lines and poles.
"While we have not had time to review the rate order in detail, it appears to strike a fair balance between the interests of our customers and shareholders," said PSI president John Mutz.
